aggressive_definition: Fatal prostate cancer incidence ('fatal disease'); the abstract also mentions analyses by stage and grade without defining their categories.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Comparing the highest (median of 855 mL/day) versus lowest (median of 103 mL/day) consumers of coffee and tea (450 vs. 12 mL/day) the HRs were 1.02 (95% CI, 0.94-1.09) and 0.98 (95% CI, 0.90-1.07) for risk of total prostate cancer and 0.97 (95% CI, 0.79-1.21) and 0.89 (95% CI, 0.70-1.13) for risk of fatal disease, respectively.
study_design: Prospective cohort study in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Among 142,196 men, 7,036 incident prostate cancer cases were diagnosed over 14 years of follow-up.
reason: The cohort abstract reports incident total prostate cancer and risk of fatal prostate cancer, an aggressive lethal-incidence endpoint, among men followed prospectively.

estimate_classifications.reason: The existing tea estimate of 0.98 (95% CI 0.90-1.07) is explicitly the total prostate cancer result; the separate tea estimate for fatal disease is 0.89.
